Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:10:1.hebrew: בעולה היא - וסקילה בבתולה כתיבא (דברים כ״ב:כ״ג): כי יהיה נערה בתולה מאורשה לאיש וגו'. ודרשינן (כתובות דף מח:): בתולה — ולא בעולה, שהבעולה בחנק כשאר אשת איש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:10:1.english: She is a non-virgin - But stoning is written [only] regarding a virgin (Deuteronomy 22:23): "If there be a girl, a virgin, betrothed to a man…" And we expound (Ketubot 48b): "a virgin" — and not a non-virgin, for a non-virgin [is punished] by strangulation, like any other married woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:10:2.hebrew: שלא כדרכה - דאיתקוש משכבות להדדי, דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:י״ג) "משכבי אשה", שתי משכבות, וקרינא בה "כי יקח" "ובעלה", ואכתי בתולה היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:10:2.english: In an atypical manner - For the [different types of] intercourse are compared to one another, as it is written (Leviticus 20:13): "the lyings of a woman," [implying] two [types of] lying. And we read concerning her, "when he takes" and "and he has relations with her," and she is still a virgin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:11:1.hebrew: א"ל אביי - ליכא לאוקמי הכי, דאי בא עליה ארוס שלא כדרכה, תו לא הויא בסקילה. דעד כאן לא פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי גבי באו עליה עשרה שלא כדרכה, ואמרו כולן בסקילה, אלא באחר שאינו בעלה; אבל בעלה עושה אותה בעולה בשלא כדרכה, דילפינן לה מבעולת בעל, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:11:1.english: Abaye said to them - It is not possible to establish [the verse] in this way, for if her betrothed had relations with her in an atypical manner, she would no longer be [subject to] stoning. For the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] only in the case where ten men had relations with her in an atypical manner and all of them [are said to be liable] to stoning — and that is [only] with regard to another man who is not her husband. But a husband renders her a non-virgin through atypical intercourse, as we derive this from the case of a woman who was [previously] intimate with her husband, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:11:2.hebrew: שלא כדרכה - דאיתקוש משכבות להדדי, דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:י״ג) "משכבי אשה" — שתי משכבות — וקרינא בה "כי יקח" "ובעלה", ואכתי בתולה היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:11:2.english: In an atypical manner - For the [two types of] intercourse are compared to one another, as it is written (Leviticus 20:13): "the lyings of a woman" — [implying] two [types of] lying. And we read concerning her [the verses] "when he takes" and "and her husband"; yet she is still a virgin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:12:1.hebrew: ועדיין היא בתולה - שבאו כולן עליה שלא כדרכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:12:1.english: And she is still a virgin - For all of them engaged in intercourse with her in an unnatural manner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:12:2.hebrew: הראשון בסקילה - לקמן יליף טעמא בשמעתין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:12:2.english: The first [is punished] by stoning - Below, in this discussion, [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:13:1.english: You find it - That there is a case of stoning.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:13:2.hebrew: שקידשה בשטר - וההיא לא בעיא ביאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:13:2.english: That he betrothed her with a document - And that [betrothal] does not require intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:13:3.hebrew: דהואיל וגומר ומוציא גומר ומכניס - בלא ביאה. הלכך, אם לאו דר' יוחנן הוה אמינא לגבי כסף, עד דמקדש ובעיל. אבל השתא דנפקא לן מבעולת בעל דבבעילה לחודה מיקדשה, ע"כ כי יקח דיליף קיחה קיחה, אגמריה דבכסף לחודה מיקדשה. דאי עד דמקדש ובעיל, כסף מאי אהני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:13:3.english: For since it completely removes, it completely brings in - without intercourse. Therefore, were it not for [the teaching] of Rabbi Yoḥanan, I would have said with regard to money [betrothal] that [she is not a fully betrothed woman] until he betroths her and has intercourse with her. But now that we have derived from [the verse] "a married woman" that she is betrothed through intercourse alone, [we must say] that when [the Torah] says "when he takes," which [Rabbi Yoḥanan] derives through the analogy of "taking" "taking," it taught us that she is betrothed through money alone. For if [it required] both betrothal and intercourse, what would the money accomplish?

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:17:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלא אשמעינן אלא קידושי ביאה, לכתוב "ובעל"; מאי "ובעלה"? זו שמעינן, ולא אמה העבריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:17:1.english: If so - that [the verse] teaches us only betrothal through intercourse, let it write "and he engages in intercourse"; what is "and he engages in intercourse with her"? [This teaches] this [case, i.e., an ordinary woman is betrothed through intercourse], but not a Hebrew maidservant.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:19:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלקידושי ביאה ולמעוטי אמה ותו לא, יליף מינה? לכתוב "או בעלה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:19:1.english: If so - That the verse comes to teach only about betrothal through intercourse and to exclude a maidservant, and nothing more, is derived from it? [If so,] let it write "or [if] he engages in intercourse with her":

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:19:2.hebrew: מאי ובעלה - משמע דקאי נמי אקיחה, למילף הך דבר אהינא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:19:2.english: What is "and engages in intercourse with her"? - It implies that it also refers to "taking," so as to derive this matter from this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:1:1.hebrew: יציאה בעינן לשמה - דכתיב (דברים כד) "וכתב לה" — לשמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:1:1.english: We require [that] leaving [be] for her sake - As it is written (Deuteronomy 24): "And he shall write for her" — [meaning,] for her sake.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:1:2.hebrew: הוייה דכסף לא בעינן שתהא לשמה - שתהא צורת הדינר טבועה לשמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:1:2.english: Becoming [betrothed] with money, we do not require that it be for her sake - that the image of the dinar be stamped for her sake.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:21:1.hebrew: האי סברא - דאין אחר עושה אותה בעולה שלא כדרכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:21:1.english: This reasoning - That no other [man] renders her a non-virgin through unnatural intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:2:1.hebrew: הדר פשטה - "ויצאה והיתה", שהרי עיקר הלימוד שהשטר קונה באשה, מכאן למדנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:2:1.english: Then he resolved it - [From the verse] “And she departs… and becomes,” for the main [source] that a document acquires a woman, we learned from here.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:3:1.hebrew: שלא מדעתה - קודם הכתיבה לא נמלך בה, ואח"כ הודיעה וקבלתה. ובגדולה קאי, והוא הדין בקטנה ונערה — לשמה ושלא מדעת אביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:3:1.english: Without her consent - Before the writing, he did not consult her, and afterward he informed her and she accepted it. This refers to an adult woman, but the same law applies to a minor girl or a *na'arah*: [if it was written] for her sake but without her father's consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:3:2.hebrew: מה יציאה שלא מדעתה - שהרי על כרחה היא מתגרשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:3:2.english: Just as leaving [is] without her consent - For she is divorced against her will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:4:1.hebrew: דעת מקנה - היינו בעל שהקנה אותה בגט זה לעצמה ופוטרה ממנו, ובעינן שיכתוב מדעתו, דכתיב "וכתב לה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:4:1.english: The consent of the one transferring ownership - This is the husband, who transfers her to herself by means of this bill of divorce and releases her from himself; and we require that he write it of his own volition, as it is written (Deuteronomy 24:1): “And he writes for her.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:4:2.hebrew: אף כאן דעת מקנה - דהיינו האשה, שנקנית לבעל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:4:2.english: So too here, the consent of the one transferring [ownership] - That is, the woman, who is acquired by the husband.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:5:1.hebrew: מאי לאו שטרי אירוסין ממש - כגון "בתך מקודשת לי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:5:1.english: What, [is it] not actual documents of betrothal - such as [a document stating], "Your daughter is betrothed to me."

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:5:2.hebrew: שטרי פסיקתא - התנאים שביניהם, וממון שפוסקין זה לזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:5:2.english: Documents of stipulation - The conditions between them, and the money that they stipulate to one another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:6:1.hebrew: באמירה - בלא קנין, שהקידושין הן גמר הדבר, דבההיא הנאה דקא מתחתני אהדדי, גמרי ומקני. ובאותן התנאים קאמר, שהעדים אין רשאין לכתוב עליהם שטר אלא מדעתם, דניחא להו שתהא כמלוה על פה ולא כמלוה בשטר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:6:1.english: Through speech - Without a formal act of acquisition, for the betrothal is the finalization of the matter: for through that benefit of their becoming related by marriage to one another, they resolve and transfer ownership. And it is with regard to these conditions that [Rav] spoke, [in which] the witnesses may not write a document concerning them except with the [parties'] consent, since they prefer that it be like an oral loan and not like a loan [recorded] in a document.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:7:1.hebrew: אמר קרא בעולת בעל - "כי ימצא איש שוכב עם אשה בעולת בעל":
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:7:1.english: The verse states: "a married woman [be'ulat ba'al]" - "If a man be found lying with a woman who is married [be'ulat ba'al]" (Deuteronomy 22:22).

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:7:2.hebrew: כעורה זו - בתמיה: וכי אינה מקובלת עליך, שאתה מחזר ללמדה ממקום אחר?
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:7:2.english: Is this one unacceptable - [Said] as a rhetorical question: Is it not accepted by you, that you go around to derive it from another place?

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:8:1.hebrew: עד דמקדש - בכסף, והדר בעיל, כדכתיב "כי יקח" — דהיינו כסף — והדר "ובעלה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:8:1.english: Until he betroths - with money, and afterward has intercourse, as it is written, “When [a man] takes” — that is, money — and afterward, “and has intercourse with her.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:9:1.hebrew: א"כ - דהכי קאמר קרא: דבעינן כסף וביאה, ובלאו ביאה לא מקדשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:9:1.english: If so - For this is what the verse is saying: that we require both money and intercourse, and without intercourse he does not betroth her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:9:2.hebrew: נערה מאורסה דבסקילה כו' - הלכך ע"כ, הא דכתיב כי יקח, הוו קידושין לעצמן, ובעלה הוו קידושין לעצמן בלא כסף, ומשכחת סקילה בקידושי כסף בלא ביאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 9b:9:2.english: A betrothed young woman, who is punished by stoning, etc. - Therefore, necessarily, [the words] "when he takes" are a betrothal in themselves, and "and he engages in intercourse with her" is a betrothal in itself, without money; and [the case of] stoning is found with betrothal by money, without intercourse:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 9b:6:1.hebrew: הן הן הדברים הנקנים באמירה - תימה: דבפרק שני דייני גזירות (כתובות קט.) תנן: הפוסק מעות לחתנו ופשט לו את הרגל — תשב עד שתלבין ראשה. ולמה תשב? ישאנה, ויקרא חמיו לדין, כיון דהן הן דברים הנקנין באמירה! וי"ל שהחתן אינו רוצה לטרוח בב"ד ולמיקם בדינא. ורשב"ם פי' דדוקא כשמתוך התנאים עמדו וקדשו, אז נקנים באמירה, ומדקדק מדקתני "עמדו"; וההוא דשני דייני גזירות מיירי בשלא קדשו מתוך הדברים, ומ"מ מאחר שהסכימו על כך — תשב עד שתלבין ראשה. ומיהו אין ראיה מלשון "עמדו", דאורחיה דגמרא בהכי, כמו "קטנה שלא מיאנה (והגדילה) ועמדה ונשאת" ביבמות פ' ב"ש (יבמות דף קח.). ור"ת פי' דהא דאמר נקנים באמירה — בנישואין ראשונים דוקא, שהאב משיא את בתו ויש לו קירוב דעת גדול אצל חתנו; אבל התם מיירי בשניים. וכן היה אומר ר"ת: אין נקנין באמירה אלא כשהאב פוסק, אבל אחיה ואמה לא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 9b:6:1.english: "These are the matters that are acquired through speech" - It is puzzling: for in the chapter Shnei Dayyanei Gezeirot (Ketubot 109a) we learned: One who stipulates a sum of money for his son-in-law, and [the father] then withdrew his foot [i.e., backed out] — she shall sit [unmarried] until her hair turns white. But why should she sit? Let [the groom] marry her, and let his father-in-law be summoned to court, since these are the matters that are acquired through speech! And one can answer that the groom does not want to trouble himself in court and to stand in litigation. And Rashbam explained that it is specifically when they arose and betrothed on the basis of the stipulations that [the items] are acquired through speech, and he infers this from the fact that [the Gemara] teaches "they arose." And that [Mishnah] in Shnei Dayyanei Gezeirot is speaking of a case where they did not betroth on the basis of the statements; nevertheless, since they agreed on this, she sits until her hair turns white. But there is no proof from the wording "they arose," for this is the Gemara's usual manner, like "a minor girl who did not refuse [her marriage], (and grew up) and arose and married," in Yevamot, chapter Beit Shammai (Yevamot 108a). And Rabbeinu Tam explained that what [Rav] said, that they are acquired through speech, applies only to first marriages, where the father marries off his daughter and has great closeness of mind with his son-in-law; but there [in Ketubot] it is speaking of second marriages. And so Rabbeinu Tam would say: [Items] are acquired through speech only when the father stipulates, but not her brother or her mother.
